reason: Both use the same weak banner layout: the dark brand block crops the sun logo and leaves SOLSTICE tiny and off-centre, 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' drifts below the dark block, 'Ships late June' breaks onto three lines one word at a time, the legal text is too small to read and is jammed against the right edge, and the CTA is a small button that is outweighed by the body copy. B is worse: its CTA label is squeezed together ('Reservea Case') and the button sits on top of the start of the legal text, a collision that A avoids by stacking them cleanly.

A keeps the original structure: a full-width header, and the eyebrow, headline, rule, body, CTA and 'Ships late June' grouped tightly. Its flaws are a large dead band between the header and the eyebrow, uneven vertical balance, and tiny legal text. B has a broken header bar that no longer reaches the canvas edges (a gap at left, cut short at right). It also pulls the eyebrow away from the headline and leaves 'Ships late June' floating far below the CTA, which breaks proximity and grouping.

Both candidates use the same broken layout. All the content is crammed into the left half and the right half is empty dead space. The orange divider is stranded alone in the middle of the right half, away from the headline it is meant to separate, and the legal line is pushed off to the bottom right as tiny, stray text. A is worse because the dark header band stops partway across, at the edge of the text column, so the canvas looks half-finished. B keeps the full-width header, so at least the brand bar survives the resize.

The two candidates are identical apart from the red 'LONGEST DAY SALE' banner. In A it sits low and its right end runs into the translucent decorative circle, which looks like an accidental collision. In B it sits clear of the circle, just under the logo. Both share the same serious flaws. The subcopy, CTA and legal text are crammed into one bottom row, and the legal text is pushed into the dark-red circle at the right edge, where it is low-contrast and almost touches the edge. The banner has shrunk from the original's hero element to a small sticker. The left-centre is empty dead space, the logo, bottle and copy blocks don't line up on any shared edge, and the hierarchy is weak.

A puts the legal line between the headline and the CTA, set far too large and almost touching the headline descenders, with an orphaned 'Co., 2026.' second line, so the fine print competes with the message and breaks the reading order. The logo (top right) and the sale banner (top left) are also split apart. B keeps the order headline → CTA and moves the legal text to the side of the CTA, but its alignment is mixed: the headline is centred, the CTA is left-aligned and the legal text is centred in a right column. The product also floats alone in the top right, away from the headline, and the big circle sitting behind the headline makes that area look muddy.

Both share the same flaws: the headline is broken into five ragged lines with 'little' stranded alone, 'botanicals' runs nearly edge to edge, and the type block is jammed close to the top while the CTA sits tight to the bottom. A spreads the subhead roughly evenly between headline and button, like the original. B pulls the subhead up under the headline, which leaves a dead orange gap of about 125px above the CTA and makes the canvas look top-heavy.

Both rewrap the headline well into four balanced lines and keep the colours, serif type and dark pill CTA intact. A's CTA sits closer to the headline, like the original, and reads as one group. B pushes the button down to about 50px from the bottom edge, which leaves a wider gap under the headline and weakens the grouping. Both are a little bottom-heavy, with about 170px of empty orange at the top.

The two are almost identical. In both, the headline's left edge (~x65) doesn't line up with the logo and subhead (~x77), and the headline runs to within ~30px of the right edge. The CTA floats to the right under the subhead, and the flavour chips sit stranded below it with dead space at the bottom, so the reading order reads headline → button → chips. A keeps SOLSTICE closer to the headline, which groups them slightly better than B, where the wordmark floats higher with a loose gap.

A: the CTA starts at x≈124 while the left text edge is at x≈74, and it almost touches the subhead. The three flavour chips sit at the bottom in a broken stagger (Cucumber Mint alone above, the other two below, so the original order is lost), with a large dead gap between the CTA and the chips. B: it has the same misaligned CTA, also jammed under the subhead, and the chips are jumbled (Blood Orange sits vertically between the other two) and crowded right under the CTA. Still, the chips stay grouped with the message and legal text, which reads better than A's split, though the lower third is left mostly empty apart from the corner circle.

A: the product circle is cut off at the top-left canvas edge and the can inside it is tiny. The NEW badge and Try It button sit between the headline and its subcopy, which breaks the reading order. Everything is packed into the top two-thirds, leaving the bottom third as dead orange space. B has a better left-to-right structure (headline, then copy, then CTA), but it breaks the product art. The cream circle is split off and left as a clipped blob in the bottom-left corner. The orange can now sits straight on the orange background, so it all but disappears; only its label band and the green dots stay visible. The NEW badge floats alone in the top-right corner, away from the product, and the headline is undersized for the canvas. A keeps the product graphic intact, so it is slightly less broken.

Both share the same flaws. The RSVP CTA is shrunk to pill size and lost among the tag chips, so the action is buried. The large italic subtitle competes with the headline. The 'SOLSTICE' wordmark reads 'SOLST CE', with a background dot breaking it. The legal text is unreadably tiny, and the broken missing-asset placeholder still shows at the bottom right. B edges ahead: its 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' kicker sits directly above the headline, and the date and time are grouped tightly. A strands the kicker up beside the logo and leaves a large gap between 'Saturday 21 June' and the time line.

A puts 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' under the headline, so the reading order is backwards. Its 'RSVP Free' CTA is the same size and colour as the 'FREE ENTRY' pill in a 2x2 grid, so the CTA doesn't stand out. The subhead and date are squeezed into narrow columns, the fine print is unreadably small and the missing-asset placeholder is still visible. B keeps the kicker above the headline. But the 'RSVPFree' CTA is merged into a stack of four pills that runs from the top edge to the bottom edge, with a missing space in its label and no hierarchy. B also has tiny fine print and the same placeholder, so it is only slightly less broken than A.

The two are almost the same layout, and both split the three badge pills: FREE ENTRY sits alone under the date block while ALL AGES and TASTINGS float above the CTA. Both also push the date block against the left edge and crowd the date, badges and CTA into the bottom half. A sits higher, which leaves dead space at the bottom, and its 'Reserve a spot' line runs straight into the partner-mark box on the same baseline. B lowers the group so the URL line sits below the partner box instead of beside it, and the vertical spacing is slightly more even.

A: the logo roundel is inflated into a big disc wedged between a tiny, illegible product bag and the body copy. It competes with the headline, dwarfs the product, and leaves the right half a cramped jumble (bag, logo, copy and CTA jammed together), while the headline breaks badly ('on / repeat'). B reads cleanly left to right (logo+headline, copy, CTA, product), but the SAVE badge floats untethered above the body copy, the product is cropped at the right edge, and the gap between headline and copy is large and uneven.

Both use the same weak stack: the subcopy is indented to x≈123, so it doesn't line up with the left-aligned headline. The LIMITED badge and the Enter Now button are jammed side by side with mismatched baselines and left edges, so they read as one cramped row, not a clear CTA. A pushes everything into the top two-thirds and leaves roughly the bottom 250px as dead space, which makes it badly lopsided. B shifts the same stack down so the weight sits near the middle and is much better balanced, but it still has the alignment and CTA-grouping flaws.

Both use the same broken skyscraper layout. The giant one-word-per-line headline takes most of the canvas. The CTA sits above the price cards and the subhead, so the reading order is reversed. The three price cards shrink to unreadable thumbnails, with YEARLY moved out of its central featured spot to the end. The legal text is cramped at the bottom. A's dark yearly card is also slightly oversized and off the shared top edge of the other cards, so B's evenly aligned row is marginally cleaner.

Both share the same faults. The dark logo panel is cropped so the sun icon is cut off and the SOLSTICE wordmark is tiny. 'Ships late June' breaks into a cramped three-line sliver. The legal text is about as large as the body copy and is jammed against the right edge, and the CTA is a small pill squeezed into the top-right corner next to it. B is slightly better because its button is fully formed with even padding, while A's button looks clipped and tight at the top edge.

Both use the same headline, set big enough to almost touch the side edges. It breaks into five ragged lines ('and a' / 'little') with a 'little' that looks orphaned, and the CTA is pushed to the bottom edge. A puts 'Now in four flavours.' right under the headline, which leaves a large dead gap above the CTA. B places the subline about midway between the headline and the button, so the vertical rhythm is more even, though the subline drifts a little away from the headline.

A and B are almost the same, and both have the same flaws. The headline runs to within about 30 px of the right edge. The left edges don't line up: the headline starts at x≈65, but the logo and subcopy start at x≈76. The CTA floats on its own at the right, under the end of the subcopy. The flavour chips sit in a separate band below it, with a large empty gap above them on the left. The pink circle is crammed into the top-right corner. The only difference is the SOLSTICE wordmark. B sits it closer above the headline, so the brand-to-headline group is tighter. In A it floats higher with a looser gap, so B is marginally better.

Both put the headline above the SOLSTICE wordmark, so the brand-first reading order is inverted, and 'Garden-fresh' crowds into the green circle at the top. Both also leave a dead gap between the body copy and a shrunken can, while the CTA is oversized next to the small product. A is slightly worse because its body copy sits jammed under the wordmark with no breathing room; B spaces that block a little more evenly.

Both use the same left-to-right banner reflow, but the decorative circles become two stacked blobs stuck to the left edge, the 'SINGLE ORIGIN' label on the bag is too small to read, CITRINE floats at mid-height with no tie to the headline, and the CTA sits off-axis from the bag. A leaves about 88px empty at the right, and CITRINE sits tight against the green circle. B moves everything right, which leaves a dead gap between the circles and the logo and pushes the headline to about 32px from the right edge. That makes B slightly more lopsided, so A is a little better.

Both use the same two-column layout, and both share the same flaws. The body copy is jammed directly under the headline with no divider or breathing room. The orange divider rule ends up orphaned above the CTA in the right column. The CTA column floats in empty navy with dead space below it. A keeps the original's full-width white header band, but the logo sits off-centre at the left. B cuts the white band off at about two-thirds of the width, so it reads as a broken, truncated panel with a stray navy notch at top right. That damages brand fidelity and balance more than A's off-centre logo.

A keeps a clear centred stack, but the headline wraps with 'last' orphaned on its own line. The legal line is nearly body size, sits between the subhead and the CTA, and is jammed against both, while the CTA pill is oversized. B splits into an awkward two-column layout. The small bottle is stranded upper-left with dead space in the middle. The subhead and legal text are squeezed into a narrow right column with ragged 2–3-word lines, and the legal text competes with a now-undersized CTA. The giant headline runs into the bottom edge, and the reading order is muddled.

The two layouts are nearly identical. In both, the can is shrunk to a tiny icon, the SOLSTICE logo is barely legible, and the tilted LONGEST DAY SALE ribbon is jammed into the lower-left corner apart from the brand. The legal copy wraps to three lines in the right column, nearly as big as the CTA label, and runs into a background dot. B wins narrowly because its Claim the Deal button lines up with the legal block's left edge, while A's button sits further left, out of alignment and crowding the headline.

A: the headline is bold, but it runs to four ragged lines and sits close to the top edge. Its axis doesn't line up with the bottom row, where the tiny italic subline is pushed against the left edge and the CTA against the right, so the grid feels arbitrary and the subline is close to illegible. B: it keeps the original's centred stack and reading order with a clean CTA. However, the headline is undersized and the subline is set almost as large as the headline and broken onto two lines, so hierarchy weakens, and the headline-to-subline gap is cramped.

A: the whole block sits too high. The headline nearly touches the top edge (about 45px) while about 110px of empty orange is left below the CTA, so the layout is top-heavy. The headline also breaks into five ragged lines with 'little' alone on its own line, and the italic subline is squeezed tight under 'sunshine.' B: same type, wrapping and orphaned 'little', and the subline is still cramped against the headline. But B's block is centred vertically, with even margins above and below, so it reads as deliberately placed. That makes B the better resize, though both need the headline line breaks reworked.

A and B look pixel-identical, so this is a tie. Both have the same problems. The legal disclaimer is blown up into a large right-hand block about as prominent as the headline. The SOLSTICE wordmark has dropped below the headline. The subtitle is shrunk to an unreadable sliver at top-left. The Blood Orange pill is a tiny fragment jammed under the Shop Flavours CTA, and the Honey Rosemary and Cucumber Mint pills are crowded against the headline block. The result has broken hierarchy, scattered groups and illegible text.

A uses the tall format well, with a large headline, a clear CTA and evenly spaced pills. But the pill order is reversed from the original (Honey Rosemary first), the pills have uneven widths, the headline nearly touches the right edge, and the gap between headline and body is too large. B crams everything into the top two-thirds and leaves a large dead area at the bottom. Its left edges are ragged: the headline is indented about 27px while the body and the Honey Rosemary pill sit at 10px, and the pills are staggered. Its decorative circles crowd the brand mark and headline.

Both layouts break the copy into scattered pieces. 'Every mixed case.' is cut off from the '20% off' it explains and sits in a top row with the CTA, the legal line floats on its own at mid-right, and the reading order jumps around (label, then subhead, then CTA, then headline below). A is worse: the circle is cropped hard at the left and bottom edges and '20% off' nearly touches the circle's sides. B pulls the circle in from the left edge and gives the headline more room inside it, but its circle is still cut off at the bottom and the grouping is just as fragmented.

A keeps the original order (headline, subline, then badge and CTA), but the subline is indented at about x=105 and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge at about x=48. The phone and its circle are crammed into the top-left corner, and the bottom 120 px or so is dead space. B has the same misaligned subline and cramped phone, and it also moves the supporting copy below the CTA. That breaks the reading order and leaves the tagline cut off from the headline it explains.

Both use the same flawed layout. The 'Sessions' headline is jammed against the bottom edge and spills past the circle. The RSVP CTA is shrunk to the size of the Free Entry, All Ages and Tastings chips and sits in a grid with them, so it is buried. The legal text is tiny and collides with the broken image placeholder. B is slightly worse: it adds a gap between the date and the time line, and pushes the 'Reserve a spot' line further from the CTA toward the right edge, which weakens the grouping.

Both scatter the content across the banner. The 'RSVP Free' CTA is shrunk to one pill in a row with the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS tags, so it is buried. The time/location line is stranded at the far right, away from the date. The secondary copy and URL are tiny left-column text. A also shows the broken red 'missing asset / partner' placeholder text crammed against the TASTINGS pill. B shrinks that placeholder to a small red stub, which is less visible, and keeps the 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' eyebrow grouped above the left column, so B is slightly less broken.

Both are near-identical 320x50 banners: the italic quote is about 7px and barely readable, the SOLSTICE wordmark/sun logo is effectively lost, the can shrinks to an unreadable orange sliver on the far right, and the yellow attribution is jammed under the quote mark, so the attribution gets more weight than the quote it credits. A also leaves a stray dot artifact (a collapsed logo/sun) under the quote, and its quote sits further left and is slightly smaller. B's quote is a little larger and cleaner with no artifact, so B is marginally less bad.

A keeps the attribution directly under the quote. But the attribution is indented from the quote's left edge and runs almost to the right edge of the canvas, there is a dead gap between the quote mark and the quote, and the logo row is crammed into the circle under the can. B makes the same indent and edge mistakes and also leaves a large empty gap between the quote and its attribution, so the credit looks like a stray fragment. Both share the same weak bottom, with an unreadable SOLSTICE label and a cramped logo.

Both are almost the same cramped leaderboard. The legal line is squeezed in tiny type beside the CTA and can't be read. The CTA nearly touches the bottom edge, and step 01 is jammed against the top edge. In A the logo sits centred over a left-aligned text column, so it is out of line with the copy, and the CTA crowds the headline. B is worse on spacing: its left margin is only about 12 px, and its enlarged coffee bag spills to the bottom edge of the canvas where A's bag sits inside the circle.

A: the oversized three-line headline dominates the left side while the body copy, a tiny CTA and legal text as big as the body are squeezed into a narrow, choppy right column. The legal text reads at nearly body size, the can floats on the left with dead space beside it, and the banner overlaps the bubble at top right, so the layout reads as two unrelated halves. B: the reading order from logo to can to headline to CTA is sound and the CTA is prominent, but the headline leaves 'last' orphaned on its own line. The legal text is jammed between the body and the CTA instead of sitting at the bottom, the banner and logo are pushed into the top corners leaving the top crowded, and the CTA overlaps the decorative circle.

Both use the same scattered three-column layout. 'Every mixed case.' sits in a top row far from the '20% off' headline it belongs to, the eye reads the subhead and CTA before the headline, and 'Ends Sunday' floats alone in the right column with a lot of dead space around it. A keeps a left margin, though its circle is cut off at the bottom. B pushes the circle hard against the left edge, cutting it off on both the left and the bottom, and '20% off' and 'WEEKEND ONLY' sit almost on the canvas edge, so B looks more cramped.

Both use the same stacked skyscraper layout. In both, the attribution starts at x≈18 while the quote starts at x≈10, so their left edges don't line up, and the quote mark doesn't align with either. Both also shrink the can to a tiny label you can't read and put the logo row on top of the purple circle's edge, right under the can. A keeps a clear gap between the quote and 'THE ULTRA TASTING TEAM', as the original does, and keeps the quote block close to its quote mark. B leaves a big dead gap between the quote mark and the quote, then jams the attribution almost against the last line ('soon.'), so the spacing feels top-heavy and cramped.

A keeps logo, eyebrow, headline and CTA on one clean left edge, but everything is crammed against the canvas edges: the logo nearly touches the top and the button nearly touches the bottom. The legal line is illegibly tiny and jammed beside the button, and the product bag runs down to the bottom edge. B has the same cramped steps and tiny legal text, and its left column is also misaligned: the logo is centred, the text is left-aligned at about 18 px and the button is indented to about 38 px, so the three elements share no common edge and look arbitrary.

A's reading order is broken: the 'Find a Store' CTA sits at the top above the headline, the SOLSTICE wordmark is wedged under the headline, and the can is pushed to the bottom over dead space, with the subhead running almost edge to edge. B has a clear structure: logo top-left, can on the green circle, a dominant headline, then the CTA at the bottom right. Its flaws are that the subhead is tiny and sits on the peach circle in the bottom-left corner, the can is crowded against the top edge, and the logo floats alone in an empty left area.

A shrinks the bottle to a tiny icon jammed in the top-right circle, so the key product is lost. The headline breaks to leave 'fizz' orphaned on its own line, and the body copy is crammed into the bottom-left corner over the peach circle, close to the edge. B keeps the bottle large and layered over the circle, with a clear left-image, right-text banner layout. But the SOLSTICE wordmark sits below the headline at nearly the same weight, which breaks the reading order and makes the two compete. 'fizz' is still orphaned, and the right-hand column is tight.

Both look the same: the long headline is crammed into four lines of a 90px-tall leaderboard, the body copy is around 7px and can't be read, and the 'Reserve a Case' button is tiny and pushed against the right edge. The white logo panel takes up a lot of width while the logo and the 'Limited Summer Release' label inside it are small. Neither cuts the body copy for this banner format, so both are cramped strips of illegible text.

The two are almost the same and share the same flaws. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow has moved below the headline, which breaks the reading order, and it has shrunk to unreadable micro-type. The orange divider is stranded under the legal text at the bottom. The logo is tiny. The body copy is set nearly as large as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy, and the legal text is so big that it fills the lower third. The only differences are minor: B leaves a slightly bigger gap between the eyebrow and the headline, and the two wrap the legal text a little differently. Neither difference is meaningful.

A puts the CTA first on the far left, which inverts the reading order. It also shrinks the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon into an unreadable sticker crammed against the subcopy, and the legal text is set as large as the subcopy with almost no gap above the tiny logo. B keeps the brand → ribbon → bottle → headline → CTA order and keeps the ribbon readable, but the headline is squeezed into three tall lines, and the legal text is a cramped six-line column jammed against the right edge at the same size as the subcopy.

The two are nearly identical. Both read left to right: logo, phone, headline, CTA. Shared flaws in both: the tilted 'LONGEST DAY SALE' ribbon runs off the left edge and floats unanchored below the logo; the decorative circles are cropped into the top-left corner; '25% off on June 21.' is squeezed against the CTA and wraps awkwardly; the legal block is tiny, crammed against the right edge and visually competes with the CTA; the phone nearly touches the bottom edge. A is very slightly better because its ribbon sits higher with more room. In B the ribbon drops toward the bottom edge, which makes the lower-left corner more cramped.

Both break the original's structure in the same ways: the green circle is split off from the can and the body copy sits on top of it. The SOLSTICE wordmark lands below the headline, so the reading order is wrong. The CTA and the two badges are squashed into a strip where they almost touch, and the tiny SUMMER ONLY badge competes with the CTA. B is worse because its body copy is jammed against the left canvas edge (about 4px margin), the circle is cut off on the left, and about 160px on the right is left empty. A at least keeps even side margins, though it wastes about 80px at the far left.

A shrinks the hero product and circle to a tiny icon at the top, so the key imagery is effectively lost. Its right column also runs in the wrong order: CTA first, then three pill badges stacked like buttons, then the body copy jammed into the bottom-right corner, far from the headline it supports. B keeps the product circle at a usable size and pairs it well with the headline on the left, but its right column has the same jumbled order (CTA above the badges, body copy last and cramped into the corner), and the tilted Free Delivery pill dropped into the stack looks accidental.

Both share the same structural flaws. The centred SOLSTICE wordmark sits above a left-aligned headline. 'back' is orphaned on its own line. There is a dead band between the headline and the phone. Both badges have been pushed below the CTA, which breaks the original reading order. A keeps the badges as a tight pair and the brand close to the headline, but its tagline floats alone in the gap between the phone and the CTA. B groups the tagline with the CTA better, but leaves SOLSTICE stranded far above the headline and spreads the two badges apart with a large gap, so the bottom reads as scattered fragments.

A keeps the original structure: the GLACIER wordmark, a one-line headline, the subhead, the pills in order and the legal line all survive. Its flaws are that the CTA is jammed right against the end of the subhead, it overlaps the lower decorative circle, and the bottom-right is a bit empty. B shrinks the GLACIER logo into a tiny label inside the circle, wraps the headline onto two lines, and makes the CTA oversized and pill-shaped so it competes with the headline. The flavour pills are stacked in reverse order and squeezed in beside the CTA, the legal text is wedged into the right edge over a circle, and the bottom row is crowded with competing focal points.

A keeps the eyebrow and headline together at the top, but the body copy is stranded far left at mid-height, the peach circle is left alone in the top-right corner, separated from the can it used to frame, and the legal line is unreadably small. B keeps the can on its circle, but its layout is scattered across three columns: '20% off' sits below its own supporting copy, the eyebrow floats far above the headline, and the CTA sits in a different column from the headline, so the reading order is jumbled. B's legal text is also too small to read.

Both are almost the same layout. In both, the peach circle is a large empty area with the shoe pushed to its lower-left edge, 'Every mixed case.' is squeezed into three lines next to the CTA so it looks like an orphan, and the legal line is shrunk to about 6 px, too small to read. The only difference is that B puts 'WEEKEND ONLY' tight against the top edge with a bigger gap to the headline, while A spaces the eyebrow and headline more evenly, which is slightly better.

A: the quote wraps to three cramped lines, and its last line, 'and gone too soon.', runs into the attribution line beside it. The open-quote mark floats on its own above the text, the Solstice wordmark logo is dropped, and the jar shrinks to an unreadable orange sliver at the right edge. B: the quote mark sits inline with a cleaner two-line quote that clears the attribution. B is still flawed: the copy is tiny and illegible at banner size, the logo is reduced to a stray speck under 'soon', the attribution is jammed against the bottom-left edge, and the jar is again a meaningless sliver.

The two are almost the same: in both, 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' has moved above the quote, so the credit is read before the quote and the original order is reversed. The SOLSTICE wordmark and the label on the can are shrunk to an unreadable size, the can is a tiny figure in a large maroon circle, and a dead band is left at the bottom. B only adds a few pixels of extra gap between the credit and the headline, which is not a meaningful difference.

A: steps are out of order (01 at top above the 'POUR-OVER, PROPERLY' eyebrow, 03 under the headline, 02 below the bag), the step text is shrunk to illegible micro-type, the logo has dropped to the footer and the footer legal copy is as large as the steps; the headline does at least lead the page. B is worse: the steps read 02, 03, 01, the eyebrow is wedged between steps 02 and 03, and the headline sits below its own supporting steps. B shares A's illegible step text and demoted logo.

Both use the same skyscraper layout. The coffee bag, the original's hero image, is shrunk to a small thumbnail and sits beside a logo roundel of the same size, so the brand mark competes with the product. The SAVE 15% badge is jammed near the top edge, and the headline's orphan 'on' line makes it read choppily. A clusters the copy and CTA right under the thumbnails and leaves about 60px of dead space at the bottom. B spreads the elements down to a bottom margin that roughly matches the top margin, though it opens a mid-canvas gap above the body copy, so B is marginally better balanced.

The two layouts are nearly identical, and both have the same problems. 'Every mixed case.' is pushed into a cramped bottom-left corner as three one-word lines at about CTA weight, so it competes with the button. The legal line is shrunk to an illegible size and jammed under the button against the bottom edge. The big empty circle with the shoe low inside it leaves a dead middle while the bottom is overcrowded. B wins only on a small point: 'WEEKEND ONLY' sits closer to '20% off', so the eyebrow reads as part of the headline group as it does in the original. A floats it higher, away from the headline.

Both are essentially the same layout. The coffee bag has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail the same size as the logo. The logo is moved from the top-left brand spot into the middle row next to the bag, so they compete as twin focal points. The SAVE 15% badge is jammed near the top-left edge. A spreads the copy and CTA down the canvas more evenly, but leaves a loose gap between the image row and the body copy, and the CTA sits close to the bottom edge. B tucks the copy up under the image but leaves about 60 px of dead space at the bottom, so the column looks top-heavy and unfinished.

Both 320x50 banners have essentially the same layout. The logo and a tiny can sit at the left, the headline wraps with 'fizz' orphaned on its own line, and the CTA sits at the right with three lines of legal text under it at about 4px, which is unreadable. The can is shrunk to a meaningless icon, and the teal circle crowds the CTA in the top-right corner. B's CTA sits slightly closer to the top edge and its legal text wraps a little more tightly, but the difference is negligible.

Both moved the orange divider so it now floats above the eyebrow, though in the original it sat under the headline. Both also leave a big dead gap between the headline and the body copy, and both shrink the legal line until it is unreadable. A at least keeps the eyebrow tight to the headline and the CTA close to its copy, as the original does. B pulls the eyebrow away from the headline and pushes the CTA down against the fine print, so the groups fall apart and the spacing looks arbitrary.

A reads left to right: brand, a large headline, then the can in its circle. But the body copy is squeezed into a narrow six-line column at tiny size.
